question: Attribute the $0.92bn (TY2022-2024) of 990-PF grant lines that say 'DAF' or 'donor advised' but name no identifiable sponsor (bucket T0, 671 return-rows): match each line's recipient city/state/ZIP to sponsors' processing addresses in their own 990 headers (e.g. Cincinnati OH, Jenkintown PA) and read the returns' GeneralExplanation text; report how much moves into T1
conclusion_affected: PF-to-DAF total (T1 $9.43bn plus T0 $0.92bn over three years); per-sponsor PF shares for Fidelity Charitable and NPT
rationale: T0 is about 10% of the T1 total and is concentrated in a few very large lines (two lines of $292m and $141m from one foundation, labelled only 'DAF' / 'DONOR ADVISED FUND'); 27 lines named only 'DONOR ADVISED FUND' carry $150m, and several of them give a Cincinnati OH address. Address matching would move most of it to a named sponsor without guessing

question: Wind-down lag: for the 438 PF returns (TY2022-2024) whose grants to sponsors (T1-T3) were at least 50% of beginning-of-year book assets but which carried no final-return or 507(b)(1)(A) flag, check the IRS e-file index 2025-2027 for a later return; count those that file a final return within two years and those that stop filing
conclusion_affected: Share of PF-to-DAF money that is a wind-down: flagged terminations give 7.0% of T1-T3 dollars, but many conversions empty the PF in one year and file the final return later
rationale: Only 524 of the 962 return-years with T1-T3 receipts of at least 50% of BOY assets were flagged as terminating. The rest look like wind-downs on the asset test, but the flag is missing from that year. The index alone (no XML) can settle whether those foundations file again

question: Split PF grants to community foundations (T3, $4.66bn over TY2022-2024) into DAF and non-DAF: code a stratified sample of 300 grant lines by purpose text and the receiving CF's published fund lists; estimate the DAF share with a confidence interval
conclusion_affected: PF-to-DAF total under the broad definition (T1-T3 = $17.34bn, 7.4% of DAFRC contributions); CF 'PF share of DAF contributions' ratios above 30% at Boston, Atlanta, San Francisco and Minneapolis
rationale: Only 11-18% of T1-T3 dollars carry DAF wording in the purpose text. Many PF grants to community foundations fund programmes or field-of-interest funds, not DAFs, so the T3 ratios to Schedule D DAF contributions overstate the DAF inflow, some of them above 50%

question: Extend the PF-to-DAF census back to TY2021 and forward to TY2025 with the same script (frame from index_2022 and index_2026/2027); test whether the TY2022-2024 rise in T1 dollars ($2.55bn to $3.91bn) is a trend or year-specific (2024 includes one $257.5m PF grant to NPT)
conclusion_affected: Direction of PF-to-DAF flows; whether 2024's 4.2% share of DAF contributions is a peak
rationale: Three years is a short series, and the top 10 PFs give 31% of T1 dollars, so a single grant moves the yearly total. TY2021 is inside the 2021+ evidence window, and the GT mirror and IRS bulk zips cover it

question: Recall pass for ambiguous sponsor names: resolve generic or duplicated recipient names that the matcher declines (e.g. 'JEWISH COMMUNITY FOUNDATION' in CA, $137m; 'THE CHICAGO COMMUNITY FOUNDATION', $127m, a separate EIN 36-3432023 held c/o The Chicago Community Trust and outside the DAFRC panel; 'CHRISTIAN COMMUNITY FOUNDATION' in TN, $85m) using recipient city and ZIP against BMF addresses, and decide whether CCT affiliates belong in the panel
conclusion_affected: T3/T4 totals and per-sponsor shares for Chicago Community Trust and the Jewish community foundations
rationale: The matcher deliberately rejects names made only of generic words and names that are not unique within a state, so these lines sit outside every tier. The unmatched-line review lists them by dollar value

question: Sponsor-side confirmation of foundation conversions: for the sponsors with the highest PF share of DAF contributions (Jewish Communal Fund ~18-21%, DonorsTrust 10-19%, ImpactAssets 11-16%, NCF ~6-8%), look for statements in their own annual reports or 990 Schedule O about accepting private-foundation assets or conversions, robots and terms permitting, and quote them
conclusion_affected: Which sponsors depend most on PF inflows; positioning of 'foundation conversion' services
rationale: The filings show where PF money lands but not why; sponsor-published material would separate one-off conversions from recurring PF pass-through grants (the largest T1 flows come from continuing PFs, not terminations)
